reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) describes semi-coherent boundaries as unexpectedly strong and resistant to dislocation penetration, which directly contradicts the hypothesis's premise that these boundaries are prone to dislocation pile-ups causing brittleness. No evidence is provided to support Boron segregation behavior, its effect on boundary compliance, or its ability to enhance ductility in this alloy system.
premises: Semi-coherent phase boundaries in eutectic HEAs are strong enough to accommodate high stress and resist dislocation penetration
Dislocation pile-ups at these boundaries cause local stress concentrations, microcracking, and brittle failure
Boron microalloying (<0.5 at.%) will segregate to lamellar boundaries
Boron segregation reduces boundary energy and makes interfaces more compliant to dislocation transmission
This interfacial modification blunts pile-ups and enhances ductility without sacrificing strength
